item.title: WAPOSAL: a multi-regional wave dataset from satellite altimetry for significant wave height, period estimation, and wave power density
item.description:
WAPOSAL: a multi-regional wave dataset from satellite altimetry for significant wave height, period estimation, and wave power density
Sonia Ponce de León, Maria Panfilova, Andrés F. Orejarena-Rondón, Marco Restano, Roberto Sabia, and Jérôme Benveniste
Earth Syst. Sci. Data, 18, 7391–7402, https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-18-7391-2026, 2026
This study presents a high-resolution wave energy resource database across 11 maritime regions for the period 2011–2023. Using satellite altimetry, sea wave parameters were obtained and validated against wave buoy and ERA5 data. The results provide a geospatial database for the development of marine renewable energy technologies and sustainable coastal planning, supporting the transition toward specialized offshore engineering solutions.

item.title: A dataset of ground-based VCDs (O3, NO2, HCHO, HONO, SO2) and AOD observations from the hyperspectral vertical remote sensing network in China (2020–2025)
item.description:
A dataset of ground-based VCDs (O3, NO2, HCHO, HONO, SO2) and AOD observations from the hyperspectral vertical remote sensing network in China (2020–2025)
Yikai Li, Chengzhi Xing, Peiyuan Jiao, and Cheng Liu
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-743,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
We created a six-year record of air pollution over China using ground-based instruments at 53 locations. The dataset includes ozone, nitrogen dioxide, formaldehyde, nitrous acid, sulfur dioxide, and airborne particles. All observations were processed in the same way and compared with satellite and other ground measurements. The dataset provides a consistent reference for checking satellite products and studying how air pollution changes across regions and over time.

item.title: Vertical profiling of the troposphere: Innovation, optimization and application, Part I (VITAL I)
item.description:
Vertical profiling of the troposphere: Innovation, optimization and application, Part I (VITAL I)
Ulrich Löhnert, Maike Ahlgrimm, Felix Ament, Jens Bange, Kjell zum Berge, Birger Bohn, Yann Büchau, Leonie Esters, Lars van Gelder, Yohanes R. S. Ginting, Luise Helmstreit, Tobias Marke, Marcus G. Müller, Patrizia Ney, Anika Obermann-Hellhund, Andreas Platis, Bernhard Pospichal, Alexander Pschera, Anja Rapmund, Mirjana Sakradzija, Martin Schön, Jan H. Schween, Maria Toporov, and Andreas Wieser
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-784,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
Accurate weather forecasts require detailed measurements of temperature, humidity and wind. During a two-week campaign in Germany, we tested innovative instruments against established measurement techniques and satellite observations. Most ground-based instruments met international performance requirements and successfully captured daily atmospheric changes. The publicly available dataset supports improved weather forecasting and the development of future weather observation networks.
